Subject: Security exhibit + pen test window for MSA/Order Form

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for running through the commercials yesterday. As we pull the MSA+Order Form together, security has a few asks around the "security exhibit" and audit rights that I'd like to get in front of you so legal can take a look and we can avoid last-minute redlines. High level: SOC 2 evidence, pen-test window + scope, and an evidence cadence for ongoing compliance.

Quick summary of what we can provide up-front:
- SOC 2 Type II attestation (most recent report, redacted where necessary)
- Summary of controls and ownership (attached: redwood_security_measurements_v1.pdf)
- Proposed evidence cadence spreadsheet (attached: proposed_evidence_cadence.xlsx)

Questions from our side that will shape the exhibit and Order Form language:
1) For pen tests: do you require a shared staging environment with access to collect logs, or are reports-only acceptable? If staging, does Lumina need VPN/whitelisted IPs or ephemeral creds?
2) Audit right scope: are you looking for annual SOC2 + one-off inspections, or a broader unlimited inspection right?
3) Evidence cadence: is weekly evidence pull acceptable for onboarding, and then monthly/quarterly thereafter?

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync this afternoon (2–2:30pm PT) to align on the above and confirm what Lumina's procurement/legal will need for the Order Form. If that doesn't work I can share a short redline to the security exhibit for your review.

Attachments: redwood_security_measurements_v1.pdf (summary), proposed_evidence_cadence.xlsx

Thanks —
Jonas Weber

Jonas —

Appreciate the overview. A couple quick clarifications from Lumina security/procurement:

- Pen tests: our preference is for a staging instance where we can validate attack surface and see remediation timelines. We need the ability to reproduce findings, so access to logs and a point-in-time snapshot of the environment is required.
- For credentials, procurement will require a short NDA amendment before providing any access; can your legal team accept a mutual NDA addendum?
- Audit rights: we don't expect "unfettered" access but we do require the right to conduct an annual inspection or one triggered by a material incident. 30 days' notice is typical for us.

I'll attach our standard requirements to make redlines easier (attached: lumina_security_requirements.pdf).

We can do the 2pm PT sync. I will invite our security lead, Raj Patel (cc'd on the calendar invite), and someone from procurement.

Best,
Alice

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit + pen test window for MSA/Order Form — legal redline notes

Jonas / Vanessa —

Saw Alice's reply and the Lumina requirements. Quick legal take (high level) before the sync:

1) Audit rights: push to limit to periodic evidence review (SOC 2 + supporting artifacts) and allow on-site or interactive inspections only with mutually agreed scope and a maximum frequency of once per year except for security incidents. We should resist language that allows unlimited inspections or broad data export rights.

2) Pen test access: agree to provide a staging environment but require clear scope (no production data, no physical access), specified IP ranges and ephemeral creds, and a kill-switch. Also require that third-party testers sign our standard testing agreement (we have a template) and that Redwood have 30 days to remediate before sharing live exploit details outside the parties.

3) Evidence cadence: propose the following compromise in the exhibit — onboarding: weekly evidence packet for first 8 weeks; steady-state: quarterly artifacts + SOC2 annually. Lumina's procurement ask for a monthly cadence might be too frequent operationally.

4) Confidentiality / NDA: we can accept a narrow NDA amendment for access, but we must ensure it doesn't broaden the main MSA confidentiality terms.

I'll draft tracked changes to the security exhibit and the audit-rights paragraph — will attach the draft (proposed_security_exhibit_redline_track_changes.docx) to send to Alice if you want me to. Also note: if Lumina insists on production-level logging access, we should escalate to infra to discuss additional controls and possible charges.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Doe <alice.doe@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + pen test window for MSA/Order Form

Alice —

Thanks for the quick reply and for sharing Lumina's requirements. Laura has drafted redlines that I think map to a compromise. Quick plan (confirming during today's 2pm sync):

- Staging access: Redwood can stand up a staging snapshot for pen tests. Access will use ephemeral credentials scoped to the test window; logs will be available for reproduction. We will not provide production data.
- Pen-test cadence & sharing: propose a single pen-test per 12-month period with an agreed 30-day remediation window before Lumina shares findings externally. Third-party testers must sign Redwood's testing agreement.
- Audit rights & evidence cadence: onboarding = weekly packets for up to 8 weeks; steady-state = quarterly artifacts + SOC 2 yearly. For one-off incident-driven inspections, we agree to cooperate with a scoped inspection with 30 days' notice.

I attached Laura's tracked-changes exhibit for your review (proposed_security_exhibit_redline_track_changes.docx). If that looks ok to Lumina's security + legal, procurement can fold the exhibit into the Order Form and we can proceed to finalize the PO.

Proposed pen-test windows (we can pick one):
- June 7–14, 2026 (preferred)
- July 12–19, 2026

If procurement needs a PO template, I'll attach one; otherwise, I'll wait for next steps after the legal sync.

Attachments: proposed_security_exhibit_redline_track_changes.docx

Thanks —
Jonas

Jonas / Laura / Vanessa —

Thanks — the plan looks reasonable. A few procurement/security operational notes from our side:

- We will need a signed NDA addendum before providing staging credentials; procurement will prepare and share the addendum by Friday.
- Lumina expects pen-test reports to be shared with Lumina and Redwood only; we will not publish them externally. We can accept the 30-day remediation hold.
- For the PO: procurement will require estimated FTE/time for staging support and log exports; can Redwood provide a short SOW or estimated support hours to include in the PO? (A simple attachment is fine.)

I've attached our PO template for reference (PO_template.docx).

I'll confirm attendees for the 2pm call; Raj will lead the technical questions.

Best,
Alice
